items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: I took it upon myself to go and buy a whole complete set of Leedy drums like Sonny Greer and Manzie and Cab, like what they had

ctx.x: in the Cotton Club with those bands had fabulous drum outfits, gongs, chimes, vibraphones, timpanies, all kind of drums hanging around. It was a beautiful setting for those bands. Well, Stocks told Harold Oxley and Jimmie Lunsford, now, your drummer got to have some drums up there. I was sitting up there with a bass drum and one cymbal. He said, no, we used to seeing drums in here, make a beautiful setting for the band.

So went to work and I, you know, I took it upon myself to go and buy a whole complete set of Leedy drums like Sonny Greer and Manzie and Cab, like what they had, and they did set the band off. It looked beautiful, took me a day to set them up.

And so I had to pay for them. I think it was around about 1,600.00. Now, I'm making about $60.00 a week, and I got pretty burned up about that, plus Lunsford never bought any uniforms or paid for the uniforms that we wore in his band to make his band impressive.
